assessments.recommendation: Monomaterial polymer housing (e.g., unreinforced PA6 or PP) without elastomer overmolding or composite fibers.
assessments.rationale: Using a monomaterial polymer housing maximizes the ease and quality of recycling (Parameter d, Page 79) and avoids technical solutions detrimental to recycling (Parameter e, Page 79). Eliminating elastomer overmolding and composite fibers prevents contamination of the plastic recycling stream, reducing the amounts of waste generated in end-of-life treatment (Parameter r, Page 80) and minimizing the release of microplastics and nanoplastics during shredding and mechanical recycling processes (Parameter p, Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use-phase/Ergonomics perspective (which prefers elastomer overmolding for grip and vibration damping) and the Durability perspective (which prefers glass-filled composites for impact resistance and structural strength).
espr_parameters: (d) ease and quality of recycling
(e) avoidance of solutions detrimental to reuse, recycling or recovery
(p) microplastic and nanoplastic released in end-of-life treatment
(r) amounts of waste generated in end-of-life treatment

assessments.recommendation: Threaded fasteners (screws) or non-destructive, reversible snap-fits using standardized tools.
assessments.rationale: Reversible joining methods ensure easy disassembly, which directly supports the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (Parameter c, Page 79, Page 27 definitions 16, 17, 18). It avoids technical solutions (like permanent adhesives or ultrasonic welding) that are detrimental to reuse, refurbishment, and recycling (Parameter e, Page 79). Non-destructive disassembly reduces the amounts of waste generated (Parameter r, Page 80) and lowers the energy and resources consumed during end-of-life treatment (Parameter g, Page 79) by avoiding destructive shredding.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing perspective, which favors ultrasonic welding or adhesives to reduce assembly time, part count, and production costs, and the Use-phase perspective, which may prefer permanent sealing for dust and water resistance (IP rating).
espr_parameters: (c) ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing and refurbishment
(e) avoidance of solutions detrimental to reuse, recycling or recovery
(g) use or consumption of energy, water and other resources in end-of-life treatment
(r) amounts of waste generated in end-of-life treatment

options_evaluated: Modular motor with separable copper windings and magnets
assessments.recommendation: Modular motor design with easily separable copper windings and magnets.
assessments.rationale: A modular motor design allows easy separation of high-value materials (copper and rare-earth magnets), enhancing the ease and quality of recycling (Parameter d, Page 79). It avoids solutions detrimental to material recovery (Parameter e, Page 79) by ensuring that valuable metals are not lost in mixed shredder scrap. This also reduces the environmental footprint produced in end-of-life treatment (Parameter m, Page 33/80) by enabling high-purity material loops, and minimizes waste generation (Parameter r, Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing perspective due to increased complexity, higher initial bill of materials (BOM) cost, and potential assembly challenges.
espr_parameters: (d) ease and quality of recycling
(e) avoidance of solutions detrimental to reuse, recycling or recovery
(m) environmental footprint produced in end-of-life treatment
(r) amounts of waste generated in end-of-life treatment

options_evaluated: Thermal potting compounds or phase-change materials
assessments.recommendation: Passive cooling vents or a removable mechanical fan, avoiding any thermal potting compounds.
assessments.rationale: Avoiding thermal potting compounds is critical as they permanently coat electronics and housing parts, acting as a solution highly detrimental to reuse, refurbishment, and recycling (Parameter e, Page 79). Potting compounds prevent the recovery of printed circuit boards (PCBs) and plastics, significantly increasing the amounts of hazardous waste generated in end-of-life treatment (Parameter r, Page 80) and increasing the energy and resources required to process or incinerate contaminated materials (Parameter g, Page 79).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use-phase/Performance perspective, as thermal potting provides superior heat dissipation, vibration resistance, and protection against dust/moisture, which can extend the product's active lifetime.
espr_parameters: (e) avoidance of solutions detrimental to reuse, recycling or recovery
(g) use or consumption of energy, water and other resources in end-of-life treatment
(r) amounts of waste generated in end-of-life treatment

options_evaluated: Highly modular architecture with separate, easily swappable functional modules
assessments.recommendation: Highly modular architecture with separate, easily swappable functional modules (battery, motor, switch/trigger, and gearbox).
assessments.rationale: A highly modular architecture directly facilitates the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (Parameter c, Page 79, Page 27 definitions 16, 17, 18). If a single module fails, it can be replaced or refurbished without discarding the entire tool, avoiding solutions detrimental to circularity (Parameter e, Page 79). This significantly reduces the amounts of waste generated (Parameter r, Page 80) and minimizes the overall environmental footprint produced in end-of-life treatment (Parameter m, Page 33/80) by keeping intact components in circulation.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Manufacturing perspective because modular connections (plugs, internal housing partitions) increase spatial requirements, tool weight, and manufacturing costs.
espr_parameters: (c) ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing and refurbishment
(e) avoidance of solutions detrimental to reuse, recycling or recovery
(m) environmental footprint produced in end-of-life treatment
(r) amounts of waste generated in end-of-life treatment

options_evaluated: Easily removable, standardized slide-on/clip-in battery pack
assessments.recommendation: Easily removable, standardized slide-on/clip-in battery pack using standard cylindrical cells.
assessments.rationale: Batteries have a shorter lifespan than mechanical parts and represent a significant safety hazard at end-of-life. An easily removable battery pack supports the ease of upgrading, reuse, and refurbishment of both the tool and the battery (Parameter c, Page 79, Page 27). It avoids solutions detrimental to recycling (Parameter e, Page 79) by ensuring batteries are removed before shredding, preventing fires and contamination. This improves the ease and quality of recycling (Parameter d, Page 79), reduces hazardous waste generation (Parameter r, Page 80), and lowers the environmental footprint of end-of-life treatment (Parameter m, Page 33/80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Product Design/Aesthetics perspective, as an external slide-on battery pack increases the tool's size, weight, and alters its balance, and the Manufacturing perspective due to the cost of designing robust contact interfaces.
espr_parameters: (c) ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing and refurbishment
(d) ease and quality of recycling
(e) avoidance of solutions detrimental to reuse, recycling or recovery
(m) environmental footprint produced in end-of-life treatment
(r) amounts of waste generated in end-of-life treatment
